tracks.name: AI Systems
tracks.description: Training, serving and evaluating machine-learning systems.

tracks.name: Data Infrastructure

talks.title: Multi-agent planning: what actually worked
talks.speaker: Maya Iyer
talks.abstract: Why multi-agent planning is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. Expected audience: about 212 participants.

talks.title: Scaling quantized inference for small teams
talks.speaker: Maya Iyer
talks.abstract: Why quantized inference is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Expected audience: about 72 participants.

talks.title: Scaling query optimization for small teams
talks.speaker: Ximena Haddad
talks.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with query optimization and how we fixed them. Expect concrete numbers, a few failure stories and an open-source companion repo. We expect around 35 attendees.

talks.title: Lessons from long-context attention in production
talks.speaker: Farid Haddad
talks.abstract: Why long-context attention is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. We compare three approaches and explain the trade-offs we accepted. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 52 people.

talks.title: Usability testing at scale without the hype

talks.abstract: Why usability testing at scale is harder than it looks, and a design that holds up. The session ends with a checklist attendees can apply on Monday. Organizers of past editions told us to plan for around 54 people.

talks.title: Scaling GPU scheduling for small teams
talks.speaker: Hiro Byrne
talks.abstract: We share the mistakes we made with GPU scheduling and how we fixed them. No prior experience is needed, but familiarity with the basics helps. Last year a similar session drew roughly 92 people.
